verdicts.correction: Output (UTF-16-LE / UTF-16-BE / UTF-32-BE / UTF-8) re-derived from the decoded .cpy bytes and the CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-26 choice and is correct; citations OK (§8.1.3.2 2), §A.1 26)). But the program uses the COPY literal-1 form (COPY "l1c03_enc16le.cpy".), which is not in COBOL-85 (the 1985 COPY is COPY text-name-1 [OF|IN library-name-1]; literal-1 is a 2002 introduction), and no existing 85 golden uses COPY at all, so there is no corpus precedent. Either move the golden to tests/conformance/2002/ (lowest edition where every construct exists; the DOC row holds at every edition so 2002 still pins it), or keep it at 85 by rewriting the three COPYs in text-name form (e.g. COPY L1C03E16L.) with the library files named per the documented text-name-to-file mapping. Keep the .cpy files byte-exact (-text in .gitattributes).

PRIME-CODE is defined NOWHERE in the program, so the source is rejected as an undefined reference whichever Format-2 reading is taken; it breaks SR4 (data-name-1 reading) just as much as SR5. An implementation that never checks SR5 (e.g. one that accepts a record-key-name declared in a DIFFERENT file control entry, SR5's real content) still rejects this program, so the negative cannot tell SR5 enforced from not. The writer's own notes concede SR5 cannot be isolated while record-key-name declaration (SOURCE IS) is Not claimed (COBOLNET1954). Do not register this as SR5's test-ref; record the row as vacuously enforced (as the adjudicator did) and leave test-ref empty.

KF-KEY is not subject to any OCCURS clause, so KF-KEY(1) is already illegal by §8.4.2.3.3 3) ('the number of subscripts shall equal the number of OCCURS clauses', cite.py OK) regardless of SR6, so SR6 is not the only reason to reject. The .err is the generic parse error COBOL0312 "unexpected '('", which does not name this rule's violation. The writer concedes (via §12.4.5.12.3 1)) that no subscriptable key can exist, so SR6 cannot be isolated from the general subscript rule. Treat the row as structurally enforced (grammar has no subscript slot) with no golden; do not claim this negative as SR6's witness.

all_upheld_flag: 3 of 12 overturned. For every upheld golden I re-derived the output from the source and the spec, not from the .out. (1) Encodings: decoded each .cpy with its BOM; overturned on edition because COPY literal-1 is absent from 85. (2) System-names: checked every system-name / user-word pairing against §8.3.2.1 4) and §8.3.2.3.1, and checked that UPON routing follows DOC-A.1-59/189. The output lines are DATA values that a system-name binding could not produce. (3) Level-numbers: traced PERFORM 05 / 01 / 88 through the section and paragraph extents: X goes 1 then 2, the X-TWO 88 is true, N=1. (4) COBOL-WORDS: checked every literal against §7.3.10.3 SR3/SR4 (UNDEFINE targets COPY/REPLACE/END-IF/SOURCE/add are reserved; SHOW/PUTVAL/WHENIF are not reserved). Checked that the relation with two literals (WHENIF 1 = 1) is not forbidden in 2023. Checked that COPY/REPLACE/>>IF/>>SOURCE come before or after the right format switch. (5) File collating: checked that unlisted characters (space) collate after Z in REV, so an implementation that wrongly applied REV to the alternate key would get START INVALID and a different line. The program sequence REV would reverse NF. Trailing spaces from DISPLAY WS-OUT X(20) are harmless because CorpusRunnerTests uses CutRunner.Normalize, which trims trailing spaces per line. (6) Report: recomputed every column from §13.18.14.4 GR3/6/8/9 (PLUS 1 = adjacent, NOTE 2). Printable sizes: 9(3)V99=5, S999 LEADING SEPARATE=4, -ZZ9.99 on -12.34 = '- 12.34' (7), VALUE 'ABC'=3, X(4) 'PQ'=4. Checked §13.15.3 SR10/12/13/14 legality: VALUE without PICTURE, SOURCE without COLUMN, and LINE without subordinates are all legal. Ran cite.py --check on all 30+ citations: all OK. One minor mislabel: report json cites 'Any unoccupied lines on the page result in a blank line' as §13.18.35.4 7), but cite.py places it at 7) b); that text is not in the .cob header. Caveats I did NOT overturn on: (a) SR-13.18.14.3-1's row editions field says 85 only, but COL/COLS/COLUMNS do not exist at 85; the 2002 placement is right and the row's editions should be fixed to 2002,2014,2023. (b) The 85 report golden reads back with X"0A"/X"0D" hex literals, which I believe are a 2002 introduction. This is the established 85 corpus reader (pb484, pb852, pb882, pb883, pb924), so it is a corpus-wide convention question for the director, not this writer's slip. (c) The file-level COLLATING SEQUENCE being a 2002 introduction follows project consensus (2002/file_collating_seq); I could not verify it against a 2002 text.
